study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter observational cohort study
exposure: maternal body mass index (BMI) at delivery
time from skin incision to infant delivery
cohort: The study included 16,723 women who delivered via cesarean section in the United States between 2008 and 2011, with known maternal BMI at delivery, skin incision-to-delivery time, and umbilical artery pH.
finding: Maternal BMI >= 50 kg/m² was associated with a longer time from skin incision to infant delivery and higher odds of UA pH < 7.0, with BMI differentially impacting UA pH at different skin incision-to-delivery time intervals.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal BMI was associated with longer skin incision-to-delivery times during cesarean deliveries, and the effect of maternal BMI on UA pH varied at different skin incision-to-delivery time intervals.
